subject: science

parts.part_text: Most liquids that conduct electricity are solutions of ________, _______ and ________.
parts.answer_text: Most liquids that conduct electricity are solutions of acids, bases and salts.

parts.part_text: The passage of an electric current through a solution causes _________ effects.
parts.answer_text: The passage of an electric current through a solution causes chemical effects.

parts.part_text: If you pass current through copper sulphate solution, copper gets deposited on the plate connected to the__________ terminal of the battery.
parts.answer_text: If you pass current through copper sulphate solution, copper gets deposited on the plate connected to the negative terminal of the battery.

parts.part_text: The process of depositing a layer of any desired metal on another material by means of electricity is called_________.
parts.answer_text: The process of depositing a layer of any desired metal on another material by means of electricity is called electroplating.

difficulty_reasoning: Direct recall of definitions and basic concepts.

subject: science
question_text: When the free ends of a tester are dipped into a solution, the magnetic needle shows deflection. Can you explain the reason?
answer_text: The deflection in the compass needle shows that current is flowing through the wounded wire and hence, through the circuit. The circuit is complete since free ends of the tester are dipped in a solution. The solution is certainly a conducting solution. This is the reason why the compass needle shows a deflection.
final_answer: Thus, the deflection indicates that current is flowing through the solution.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of electric current and its effects.

subject: science
question_text: Name three liquids, which when tested in the manner shown in Fig. 14.9, may cause the magnetic needle to deflect.
answer_text: Liquids like lemon juice, salt water and vegetable oil allow electricity to pass through them.
final_answer: These liquids can be used to show the effect of electric current.
difficulty_reasoning: Direct recall of examples of conductive liquids.

subject: science
question_text: The bulb does not glow in the setup shown in Fig. 14.10. List the possible reasons. Explain your answer.
answer_text: The bulb may not glow because of the following reasons: (i) Liquid in the beaker is non-conducting. In such case, the electric current would not be able to pass through the liquid. Hence, the circuit is not complete. (ii) Electric current in the circuit is very weak. This can happen if the material used for making the circuit is not a good conductor of electricity or the battery does not have sufficient energy to generate electricity.
final_answer: Thus, the bulb does not glow due to non-conductive liquid or weak current.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of circuit components and conductivity.

subject: science
question_text: A tester is used to check the conduction of electricity through two liquids, labelled A and B. It is found that the bulb of the tester glows brightly for liquid A while it glows very dimly for liquid B. You would conclude that (i) liquid A is a better conductor than liquid B. (ii) liquid B is a better conductor than liquid A. (iii) both liquids are equally conducting. (iv) conducting properties of liquid cannot be compared in this manner.
answer_text: Liquid A is a better conductor than liquid B. The amount of current flowing through a conducting solution depends on the conductivity of the solution. With more conductivity, more current passes through the solution and vice-versa.
final_answer: Hence, the conductivity of liquid A is more than the conductivity of liquid B.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of conductivity and comparison.

subject: science
question_text: Does pure water conduct electricity? If not, what can we do to make it conducting?
answer_text: No. Pure water does not conduct electricity. This is because pure water is devoid of any salts. Pure water can conduct electricity when a pinch of common salt is added to it, as salt solution is conducting in nature.
final_answer: Thus, adding salt makes pure water conductive.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of conductivity and solutions.

subject: science
question_text: In case of a fire, before the firemen use the water hoses, they shut off the main electrical supply for the area. Explain why they do this.
answer_text: Water may conduct electricity. If the electrical supply for the area is not shut off and water is poured over electrical appliances, then electricity may pass through water and harm the firemen.
final_answer: That is why, in case of a fire, the firemen shut off the main electrical supply for the area before they use the water hoses.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of safety measures in electrical contexts.

subject: science
question_text: A child staying in a coastal region tests the drinking water and also the seawater with his tester. He finds that the compass needle deflects more in the case of seawater. Can you explain the reason?
answer_text: Seawater contains a higher concentration of salts compared to drinking water, making it a better conductor of electricity.
final_answer: Thus, the compass needle deflects more in seawater due to its higher conductivity.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of conductivity differences in solutions.

subject: science
question_text: Is it safe for the electrician to carry out electrical repairs outdoors during heavy downpour? Explain.
answer_text: No. It is not safe to repair electrical appliances outdoors during heavy downpour. This is because rain water contains dissolved salts. Therefore, rain water can conduct electricity. The electrician may get electrical shocks while working outdoors during rain.
final_answer: Thus, it is unsafe for electricians to work outdoors in the rain due to the risk of electric shock.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of electrical safety and the properties of water.

subject: science
question_text: Paheli had heard that rain water is as good as distilled water. So, she collected some rain water in a clean glass tumbler and tested it using a tester. To her surprise, she found that the compass needle showed deflection. What could be the reasons?
answer_text: Rain water contains dissolved salts. This makes it a conducting solution. There are no dissolved salts present in the distilled water. Hence, rain water can allow electricity to pass through it while distilled water cannot.
final_answer: Therefore, rain water conducts electricity due to the presence of dissolved salts.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding the difference between rain water and distilled water.

subject: science
question_text: Prepare a list of objects around you that are electroplated.
answer_text: Examples of electroplated objects are as follows: (i) Chromium plating is done on different parts of cars, buses and motor cycles to give them shiny appearance. (ii) A fine layer of gold is deposited on the silver ornaments and they are called gold-plated ornaments. (iii) Iron used in constructing a building is coated with a layer of zinc. This protects iron from corrosion and rusting.
final_answer: Thus, electroplating is used for various objects to enhance appearance and prevent corrosion.

subject: science
question_text: The process that you saw in Activity 14.7 is used for purification of copper. A thin plate of pure copper and a thick rod of impure copper are used as electrodes. Copper from impure rod is sought to be transferred to the thin copper plate. Which electrode should be attached to the positive terminal of the battery and why?
answer_text: Copper ion is positively charged. It is attracted towards the plate which is connected to the negative terminal of the battery. As copper ions are transferred to the thin copper plate, this thin pure copper plate must be connected to the negative terminal of the battery. Consequently, impure copper rod is connected to the positive terminal of the battery.
final_answer: Therefore, the impure copper rod should be connected to the positive terminal of the battery.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of electrolysis and electrode polarity.
